ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Low-rank cross-channel mixing after a channel-independent patch encoder
PROPOSAL: Keep a PatchTST-style channel-independent encoder with patch length 16 and lookback 336, and insert a low-rank mixing layer (rank 8) over the encoded channel tokens before a linear decoder. Train with mean squared error on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather and Electricity at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720. Report test mean squared error and mean absolute error, parameter counts and training time per epoch, and compare the gain against the cost of a full cross-channel attention layer.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unmodified channel-independent encoder, a channel-dependent iTransformer of matched parameter count, DLinear, and the mixing layer with random frozen weights. Run 5 seeds and ablate the rank over 4 and 16.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: The mixing layer should cut mean squared error by 2 to 4 percent on Electricity and Weather; it could fail on ETTh1, where the 7 channels are weakly coupled and the gain stays within seed noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-channel attention in a deep encoder for a single traffic dataset
PROPOSAL: Use a 6-layer iTransformer-style encoder with embedding size 512, where attention covers the 862 channel tokens of Traffic, followed by a linear decoder, lookback 336. Train with mean squared error and a warmup of 5 epochs followed by cosine decay at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, and retrain the full model with 5 different seeds at each horizon. Report test mean squared error and mean absolute error, parameter counts and training time per epoch, and compare channel-token attention against a version where tokens are mixed by a fixed averaging operator.
CONTROLS: Compare against the channel-independent PatchTST encoder, DLinear, a shallower 2-layer variant of the same encoder, and the attention with random frozen weights. Ablate the embedding size over 128 and 256.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Channel attention should cut mean squared error by 3 to 6 percent against the channel-independent encoder; it could fail at horizon 720, where the extra depth overfits the training years.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-attention horizon-query decoder in place of a linear projection
PROPOSAL: Replace the linear projection with a decoder where 24 learned horizon queries attend to the encoder's patch tokens through 2 cross-attention layers, then a shared linear map produces the future values. Pair it with PatchTST and iTransformer encoders, lookback 336, batch size 32, 30 epochs, and train with mean squared error on Solar-Energy, Electricity, Traffic and ETTm2 at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720. Report test mean squared error, mean absolute error and training time, and compare against a 2-layer MLP head of the same parameter count to separate depth from the horizon-query structure.
CONTROLS: Compare against the linear projection, the matched MLP head, queries that are fixed instead of learned, and the decoder with cross-attention restricted to the last 4 patches. Run 5 seeds for each encoder-decoder pair.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The decoder should cut mean squared error by 3 to 5 percent on Traffic and Electricity with the iTransformer encoder; it could fail on ETTm2, where smooth series make a linear map sufficient.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decoder depth study for a single electricity dataset with a 12-layer encoder
PROPOSAL: Use a deep PatchTST-style encoder with embedding size 768 on Electricity, lookback 336, and compare a linear projection against decoders of 1 to 8 cross-attention layers with 24 learned horizon queries. Train with mean squared error at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, running 3 seeds per configuration. Report test mean squared error, mean absolute error and training time, and compare against a 2-layer MLP head of the same parameter count to separate depth from the horizon-query structure.
CONTROLS: Compare against the linear projection, the matched MLP head, queries that are fixed instead of learned, and the decoder with cross-attention restricted to the last 4 patches. Ablate the number of queries over 12 and 48.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Deeper decoders should cut mean squared error by 3 to 5 percent up to 4 layers; it could fail beyond that, where the 8-layer decoder overfits a single dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Single-stage training with an in-loop masked reconstruction term versus two-stage pretraining
PROPOSAL: Train a PatchTST-style encoder with a cross-attention decoder in a single stage, where the loss is the forecasting error plus a masked-patch reconstruction term whose weight decays to a tenth of its start over training. Compare with the two-stage pipeline of masked pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning, using the same encoder and decoder. Evaluate on ETTh1, ETTm1, Solar-Energy, Electricity and Traffic at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, lookback 512, with test mean squared error reported.
CONTROLS: Compare against supervised-only training with the same architecture, the two-stage pipeline, single-stage training with a constant reconstruction weight. Run 5 seeds and ablate the mask ratio over 25 and 50 percent.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Single-stage training should match the two-stage pipeline within 1 percent in mean squared error at less than half of the training time; it could fail on Traffic, where the reconstruction term competes with forecasting for capacity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two-stage pretraining and fine-tuning for a pair of large datasets with repeated runs
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a PatchTST-style encoder by masked-patch reconstruction on Weather and Traffic with mask ratios of 25, 40 and 55 percent, then fine-tune with a cross-attention decoder and mean squared error, using the AdamW optimizer with a batch size of 64 and cosine decay. Compare with supervised-only training of the same architecture, using lookback 512 and horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720. Repeat the pretraining and fine-tuning with 10 different seeds per mask ratio, and report test mean squared error and total training time for each pipeline.
CONTROLS: Compare against supervised-only training with the same architecture, a linear decoder with each pipeline, pretraining on the test dataset's own training split, and pretraining with the mask placed on whole channels. Ablate the pretraining length over 50 and 100 epochs.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Pretraining should cut mean squared error by about 2 percent against supervised-only training; it could fail on Traffic, where the gain stays inside the spread of the 10 seeds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Matched-parameter comparison of channel-independent and channel-dependent encoders
PROPOSAL: Train a channel-independent PatchTST encoder and a channel-dependent iTransformer encoder with matched parameter counts of about 1.2 million on ETTh1, ETTh2 and Weather, using a linear decoder, lookback 336 and horizons 96 and 336. Measure test mean squared error and mean absolute error, and per-epoch training time and memory. Compute the difference in error between the 2 encoders and test whether it exceeds the spread across 3 seeds, to decide when cross-channel modeling is worth its cost on small datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare against DLinear and a persistence forecast, and ablate the channel-dependent encoder by shuffling channel order at test time. Check that parameter counts differ by under 5 percent.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The 2 encoders should differ by less than 2 percent on ETT data; it could fail on Weather, where 21 correlated channels may favor the channel-dependent encoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Channel-dependent encoder scaled to a larger backbone on Solar-Energy
PROPOSAL: Train an iTransformer encoder of 8 layers and embedding size 512 on Solar-Energy, with a linear decoder, lookback 336 and horizons 96 and 336, and compare it against a PatchTST encoder scaled to the same parameter count of about 9 million. Measure test mean squared error and mean absolute error, and per-epoch training time and memory. Retrain both encoders with 5 seeds, work out the difference in error and test whether it exceeds the seed spread, to decide when cross-channel modeling is worth its cost on a large series.
CONTROLS: Compare against DLinear and a persistence forecast, and ablate the channel-dependent encoder by shuffling channel order at test time. Check the 2 encoders over embedding sizes of 256 and 512.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The 2 encoders should differ by 3 to 5 percent on Solar-Energy; it could fail because solar series share one daily cycle that both encoders capture equally well.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shared patch tokens feeding both a forecasting decoder and a reconstruction decoder
PROPOSAL: Encode patch tokens once with a channel-independent encoder, then feed them to a cross-attention forecasting decoder and a lightweight reconstruction decoder trained jointly with the reconstruction weight at 20 percent of the forecasting weight. Train with mean squared error on ETTh1, ETTm2, ETTh2, Electricity, Traffic and Solar-Energy at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, lookback 512. Report test error and training time, and compare the joint model with a pipeline where the reconstruction decoder is trained first and frozen before forecasting is learned.
CONTROLS: Compare against the forecasting decoder alone, the frozen-reconstruction pipeline, a linear decoder, and PatchTST and iTransformer baselines. Run 5 seeds and ablate the reconstruction weight over 10 and 50 percent.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Joint training should cut mean squared error by 2 to 4 percent against the forecasting decoder alone; it could fail on Solar-Energy, where reconstruction of near-zero night values dominates the shared tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Encoder-decoder pairings swept on 2 datasets
PROPOSAL: Pair 5 encoders (PatchTST, iTransformer, TimeMixer, a state space encoder and a convolutional encoder) with 3 decoders (linear projection, 2-layer MLP head, cross-attention horizon queries) and train each of the 15 pairs with mean squared error on Weather and Electricity at horizons 96 and 336, lookback 512. Repeat these pairings with 3 seeds, and report test error and training time. Fit an additive model of error with terms for encoder and decoder to see whether interactions between them matter beyond the main effects.
CONTROLS: Compare against DLinear, the additive model without interaction terms, and a shuffled assignment of decoders to encoders. Ablate lookback over 336 and 720 for the best 3 pairs.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The interaction terms should explain under 20 percent of the variance in error; it could fail because the stronger decoder may gain mostly with the weaker encoders.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mamba encoder with a linear versus a multilayer decoder on solar and traffic data
PROPOSAL: Train a bidirectional state space encoder with 4 blocks on Solar-Energy and Traffic with batch size 32, lookback 336 and horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, using mean squared error. Compare a linear decoder with a 2-layer MLP decoder that maps patch tokens to horizon blocks of 24 steps. Report test mean squared error, mean absolute error, throughput and memory, and measure how error changes as the lookback is lengthened from 96 to 720, to see whether the decoder choice interacts with the length of history.
CONTROLS: Compare against PatchTST with the same 2 decoders, DLinear, and the state space encoder with its recurrent state reset at patch boundaries. Run 3 seeds and report the spread.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The MLP decoder should cut mean squared error by 2 to 3 percent at horizons 336 and 720; it could fail at horizon 96, where the linear map already fits the near-term signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Long-lookback state space encoder with decoder variants on Electricity
PROPOSAL: Train a bidirectional state space encoder with 8 blocks on Electricity with lookback 720 and horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, using mean squared error. Compare a linear decoder, a 2-layer MLP decoder and a 4-layer MLP decoder that map patch tokens to horizon blocks of 24 steps, over 5 seeds per variant. Report test mean squared error, mean absolute error, throughput and memory, and check how error moves when the lookback is lengthened from 96 to 720.
CONTROLS: Compare against PatchTST with the same 3 decoders, DLinear, and the state space encoder with its recurrent state reset at patch boundaries. Report the seed-to-seed spread.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The deeper decoder should cut mean squared error by 2 to 3 percent at horizons 336 and 720; it could fail at horizon 96, where the linear map already fits the near-term signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned channel graph applied at the decoding stage for cross-channel dependence
PROPOSAL: Predict future patch tokens per channel with a channel-independent encoder (patch length 16, stride 8), then refine them in the decoder with attention restricted to a sparse learned graph where each channel keeps its 8 strongest neighbors. Train with mean squared error on Weather, Electricity, Traffic and Solar-Energy at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, lookback 512. Report test error, training time and memory, and compare with a full channel attention in the decoder and with a graph built once from training-set correlations.
CONTROLS: Compare against a channel-independent model with a linear decoder, iTransformer, the correlation graph, and a random graph with the same neighbor count. Run 3 seeds and ablate the neighbor count over 4 and 16.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The learned graph should recover at least 80 percent of the full attention gain at a quarter of the cost; it could fail on Weather, where channels are few and full attention is already cheap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Full channel attention in the decoder at 4 scales of embedding size on Traffic
PROPOSAL: Predict future patch tokens with a channel-independent encoder, then refine them in the decoder with full attention among the channels of Traffic, at embedding sizes from 128 to 1024. Train with mean squared error at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, lookback 512, running 3 seeds per embedding size. Report test error, training time and memory, and compare with a decoder that attends to a graph built once from training-set correlations.
CONTROLS: Compare against a channel-independent model with a linear decoder, iTransformer, the correlation graph, and a random graph with the same neighbor count. Ablate the number of decoder layers over 1 and 3.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Full attention should lead the correlation graph by 3 to 5 percent in mean squared error; it could fail at the 1024 embedding size, where memory limits the batch to a few windows.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frequency-domain loss term aligned with a patch decoder
PROPOSAL: Train a PatchTST-style encoder with a patch-wise linear decoder, adding to the mean squared error a loss on the amplitude spectrum of each predicted patch, weighted 10 percent. Evaluate on ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather and Electricity at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, lookback 336. Report test mean squared error and mean absolute error, and a spectral error that compares predicted and true amplitude at the dominant 5 frequencies, to see whether the term fixes the smoothing of periodic series.
CONTROLS: Compare against plain mean squared error, an absolute-error loss, a loss on the whole horizon spectrum instead of the patch spectrum, and the same term at 5 and 50 percent of the base weight. Run 3 seeds.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The spectral term should cut the dominant-frequency error by 10 percent with a 1 percent gain in mean squared error; it could fail on ETTh1, where noise dominates the spectrum.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spectral loss with a deeper backbone for a single long-horizon setting
PROPOSAL: Train a 10-layer PatchTST-style encoder (patch length 16) with a patch-wise linear decoder on Weather, adding to the mean squared error a loss on the amplitude spectrum of the predicted horizon, weighted 0.1, at horizon 720 with lookback 720. Train the model with 10 seeds at 5 loss weights. Report test mean squared error and mean absolute error, and a spectral error that compares predicted and true amplitude at the dominant 5 frequencies, to see whether the term fixes the smoothing of periodic series.
CONTROLS: Compare against plain mean squared error, a Huber loss, and the spectral term applied to the first half of the horizon only. Report the spread of the 10 seeds.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The spectral term should cut the dominant-frequency error by 10 percent with a 1 percent gain in mean squared error; it could fail because Weather has strong daily and yearly cycles that are already well fit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint scheduling of decoder depth and horizon-block size under direct multi-step training
PROPOSAL: Train a channel-independent PatchTST-style encoder with a cross-attention decoder that emits the horizon in blocks, and vary the block size over 12, 24 and 48 steps together with 1 or 2 decoder layers. Use direct multi-step mean squared error on ETTm1, Weather, Electricity and Solar-Energy at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, lookback 512. Report test error and training time for each configuration, and compare with a recursive scheme that reuses a short-horizon decoder to roll the forecast forward, to test whether block size matters more than depth.
CONTROLS: Compare against the linear projection, a recursive roll-out of a 96-step decoder, DLinear, and block sizes assigned at random per training step. Run 3 seeds and report the spread.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: A block size of 24 should win in 3 of 4 datasets by about 2 percent; it could fail on Solar-Energy, where blocks that straddle sunrise lose the sharp onset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decoder depth and block size for a large traffic dataset with repeated runs
PROPOSAL: Train a channel-independent PatchTST-style encoder with a cross-attention decoder that emits the horizon in blocks on Traffic, varying the block size from 12 to 96 steps and the decoder depth from 1 to 6 layers. Use direct multi-step mean squared error at horizons 96, 192, 336 and 720, lookback 720, with a cosine learning-rate schedule and early stopping on validation error, and run all 16 configurations with 3 seeds. Report test error and training time per configuration, and compare with a recursive scheme that reuses a short-horizon decoder to roll the forecast forward.
CONTROLS: Compare against the linear projection, a recursive roll-out of a 96-step decoder, DLinear, and block sizes assigned at random per training step. Report the seed-to-seed spread.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: A block size of 24 should win in most depth settings by about 2 percent; it could fail for the 6-layer decoder, where the larger model overfits the training split.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lookback sensitivity of channel-independent and channel-dependent encoders with a learned decoder
PROPOSAL: Train PatchTST and iTransformer encoders with a cross-attention decoder on Weather, Electricity and ETTm1 at horizons 96 and 336, with lookback windows of 96, 192, 336 and 720. Use mean squared error, report test error and training time, and fit the slope of error against log lookback for each encoder to find where each encoder stops benefiting from longer history, and whether the decoder shifts that point.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same encoders with a linear decoder, DLinear, and a version where the lookback window is filled with repeated copies of the last 96 steps. Run 3 seeds for each configuration.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The channel-independent encoder should keep improving up to lookback 720 while the channel-dependent one flattens near 336; it could fail on ETTm1, where longer history adds noise for both encoders.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lookback sensitivity of a single encoder at several depths on Electricity
PROPOSAL: Train a PatchTST encoder with 4, 8 and 12 layers and a cross-attention decoder on Electricity at horizon 336 with lookback windows from 96 to 720. Use mean squared error, train the configurations over 5 seeds, report test error and training time, and fit the slope of error against log lookback for each depth to find where the encoder stops benefiting from longer history, and whether the decoder shifts that point.
CONTROLS: Compare against the same encoders with a linear decoder, a persistence forecast, and a version with the patch length doubled. Report the seed-to-seed spread.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Deeper encoders should keep improving up to lookback 720 while the 4-layer one flattens near 336; it could fail for the 12-layer encoder, where longer history adds noise.
